Entire-Checkpoint: 4c0baf45a2a2","messageHeadline":"fix(cli): pin render testdata goldens to LF, normalize CRLF in contra…","oid":"df01f21cff6be7d48f079cd1717326607ba61843"},{"authoredDate":"2026-08-29T17:19:33Z","authors":[{"email":"257360244+suhaanthayyil@users.noreply.github.com","id":"U_kgDOD1cBdA","login":"suhaanthayyil","name":"Suhaan Thayyil"}],"committedDate":"2026-08-29T17:19:33Z","messageBody":"The onboarding path advertised a bounded, one-command setup and then installed
a watcher that was bounded by none of it.

Spend
- brainWatchDaemonArgs emitted no --max-sessions, and watchDistillOptions never
  set maxSessions, so the daemon's gated distill was UNCAPPED. `setup` distilled
  25 sessions, printed "capped at 25 of N ... re-run setup for the next batch",
  and installed a watcher that distilled the remaining N-25 in one window, per
  repo, silently. --distill-every and the cursor bound how OFTEN the daemon
  spends; nothing bounded how MUCH. `watch` gains --max-sessions (0 = no cap)
  and setup passes the same budget it reported; a capped pass is newest-first,
  matching what setup told the user it did. Uncapped `watch --distill` is
  unchanged.
- The daemon was handed no --agent, so it used watch's "codex" default no matter
  which agent setup resolved, reported, and paid the backfill with. On a
  claude-only machine that daemon can never succeed, and since the agent name is
  in the distill cache salt, a codex installed later re-distills the whole corpus
  already paid for. The agent is now resolved ONCE, before the daemon plan is
  built, and carried into both the detached child and the unit.
- A negative --backfill-budget read as the documented 0 ("unlimited") and spent
  the whole corpus on a typo. Both the backfill and the daemon now go through one
  normalizer; only an explicit 0 means unlimited.
- `distill --force --max-sessions N` deleted deferred sessions' facts and marked
  them done. A forced pass drops every distilled fact on each branch it visits,
  and a deferred session continues before that -- so a sibling on the same branch
  had already dropped its facts while its cache fingerprint was carried through,
  making it skipped forever while `status` counted it as distilled. --session +
  --force is rejected outright for the same reason; this pair had no guard.
- The watcher charged its --distill-every window to a distill that never ran.
  withDistillPassLock returns nil on contention (right for `distill`: someone
  else is doing the work), and `setup` creates that contention by design -- an
  hours-long detached backfill plus a watcher that ticks immediately. The window
  is now handed back and the tick logs the skip instead of "spent tokens".

Availability
- --workspace was validated only inside registerRepoInWorkspace, whose failure
  setup downgrades to a warning, and the daemon was installed regardless: a
  KeepAlive/Restart=always unit running `workspace watch <name the CLI rejects>`,
  restarted every 60s forever, while setup exited 0. Rejected up front now.
- seedRefreshNeeded's error was returned raw instead of through stage(), so a
  best-effort refresh still aborted -- on the RE-RUN path, with ZERO components
  reported, no instant.json, no reason for status/doctor to print, and the
  workspace, daemon and backfill all skipped. A freshness probe that cannot run
  is a failed seed source and is reported as one.
- An unparseable setup.json read as "never set up, here are the defaults", so
  --uninstall-daemon removed the machine-wide watcher other repos depend on.
- A corrupt workspace.json wedged registration for every member with an error
  that named neither the file nor a way out.
- Re-registering a repo overwrote the whole member record, erasing a name set
  with `workspace add --name`. setup re-registers on every run.
- The backfill log is the one write here that cannot use writeFileAtomic (it is
  appended to), and it opened without O_NOFOLLOW at a predictable path.

Coverage the mutation survey proved was missing
- brainWatchDaemonPlan's single read of runtime.GOOS was executed by no test:
  pinning it to "windows" makes setup install nothing, forever, and left all 635
  package tests passing.
- setup_spawn.go had zero coverage; deleting the setsid call its own comment
  calls "the whole point" passed all 41 setup tests while making every backfill
  die with the shell that started it.
- The --json contract test re-implemented writeJSON's encoder instead of running
  it, so a change to indentation, escaping or the trailing newline passed.

Every fix has a test that fails without it.","messageHeadline":"fix(setup): make the documented spend caps actually bind on the daemon","oid":"b902dc197d9e1bcaa87bdd38b9c70c44ad4cc277"},{"authoredDate":"2026-08-29T19:12:44Z","authors":[{"email":"r@r","id":"","login":"","name":"r"}],"committedDate":"2026-08-29T19:12:44Z","messageBody":"setup.go's header states the invariant: "Running setup twice must produce the
same machine, not two daemons and two workspace entries." The daemon did not
keep it.

The identity was machine-wide -- the launchd label and systemd unit name derive
from the daemon NAME alone -- while the rendered unit was per-repo:
`workspace watch <ws> --interval ... --distill-every ... --model ... --effort ...`.
So two repos resolved to ONE unit path and rendered DIFFERENT bytes. The second
`setup` overwrote the first repo's watcher; that repo was never watched again,
and its `status` still said "running" because inspectDaemon computed the drift
(Current=false) and describeDaemonState dropped it. Two repos on the SAME
workspace clobbered each other's interval, model and effort just as silently.
--daemon-name did not help: retirement consulted only the CALLING repo's setup
record, so a second repo naming a different daemon installed a second unit that
no `status` and no --uninstall-daemon could see, ticking and distilling forever.

The unit is now workspace-independent and byte-identical everywhere: `workspace
watch --distill`, nothing else. Everything per-workspace -- interval, distill
cadence, agent, model, effort, session cap -- moves into a machine-level watch
plan the running watcher re-reads on every outer pass. `workspace watch` with no
positional argument is that supervised mode; with one, it is unchanged.

Consequences:
- A second repo's setup ADDS a row to the plan. The unit's bytes do not change,
  so inspectDaemon sees no drift and the service is never unloaded and reloaded
  under an in-flight refresh.
- The plan records which daemon name is installed, so --daemon-name MOVES the
  machine's watcher instead of forking it. A first-ever setup with a custom name
  still retires nothing.
- An empty or unreadable plan is reported and survived rather than returned as
  an error: under KeepAlive/Restart=always, exiting non-zero is a restart loop.
  One failing workspace does not stop the others.
- describeDaemonState surfaces Current, so a drifted or foreign watcher says
  "not current" and names the command that fixes it.

Also in this change, because both are the same class of silent wrong answer:

processAlive was a bare kill(pid, 0). Pids are reused and a reboot hands the low
ones straight back out, so a setup.json written before a reboot named a pid that
afterwards belonged to a system daemon: setup skipped the backfill as "already
running" for as long as that stranger lived, status reported a pass that did not
exist, and the repo's facts were never backfilled again. backfillRunning now
cross-checks the recorded pid against the distill pass lock -- pid gone means
gone, pid present with the lock held means running, pid present with the lock
free means the record is stale. The race between a child's Start() and its
acquisition of that lock is accepted and documented: a rival child is benign
because the pass lock makes the second one skip.

The backfill's cost line moved BEFORE the spend. Everything a user needs to
decide about the one phase that spends money -- what it will run, over how many
sessions, and the flag that turns it off -- was printed after the detached child
was already running.

`setup` and `status` now name the workspaces the machine's watcher covers. A
hashed launchd label answers nothing a reader came to ask, least of all right
after a second repo ran setup.","messageHeadline":"fix(setup): give the machine one watcher that watches every workspace","oid":"400980a7d3df9bcc97f2829801efb8c46289697e"},{"authoredDate":"2026-09-05T16:31:19Z","authors":[{"email":"r@r","id":"","login":"","name":"r"}],"committedDate":"2026-09-05T16:31:19Z","messageBody":"A brand-new user's very first `entire-brain setup` reported failures that had
nothing to do with their repository, and then pointed them at a command that
said nothing about any of them.

  * `session export failed (... parse checkpoint list json: invalid character
    'U' after top-level value)`. The `U` is the host `entire` CLI's
    "Update available!" banner: released versions print it on the SAME stream
    as `--json` output, so `checkpoint explain --json` emits a complete JSON
    value and then a banner, and the whole-buffer json.Unmarshal fails on it.
    The host caches its version check for 24h, so this failed on the
    first-ever run and silently healed on the second, which reads as
    flakiness. Decode the first JSON value and tolerate trailing output;
    leading garbage stays an error.

  * A missing entire-graph plugin reported only "provider_doctor_failed:
    semantic provider no-egress status is not verified". The provider doctor
    captured the real cause -- `unknown command "graph"` -- into the warning's
    Detail and it was then dropped. Surface it, shorten it to one line (a CLI
    answers an unknown command with sixty lines of usage), and name the
    install step when the plugin is simply absent.

  * `entire-brain doctor`, the command setup tells you to run when a component
    fails, gated its whole repo-scoped section on ENTIRE_REPO_ROOT -- which
    only the host sets when it dispatches the plugin. In a plain terminal it
    printed plugin-directory health and nothing else. Infer the repository
    from the working directory, and say so when there is none.

  * A pristine clone graded itself "freshness: degraded" because the host CLI
    setup shells out to writes an empty .entire/logs/entire.log inside the
    working tree. Every other reader in the brain already treats .entire as
    ignored; the live-state check read raw `git status`. Apply the same
    ignore policy there.

  * setup in a directory that is not a git repository failed four components
    with a raw `fatal: not a git repository`, registered a workspace, wrote
    per-repo state, installed the watcher, and exited 0. Refuse up front,
    before any side effect. --uninstall-daemon stays exempt.

  * --uninstall-daemon appeared only in `setup --help`. setup and status now
    name it, and setup says plainly that a persistent service was installed
    and where its unit lives. The default is unchanged.

  * ENTIRE_BRAIN_DAEMON_DIR redirects the unit FILE only; `launchctl load -w`
    and `systemctl --user enable --now` act on the caller's live session
    whatever directory the file came from, so a CI job or smoke test setting
    only that variable still registered a real KeepAlive agent. Add
    ENTIRE_BRAIN_DAEMON_NO_REGISTER, which writes the unit and withholds the
    service-manager call, and correct the comment that claimed the guarantee.

  * The watcher logged budget=0 -- the value a setup-installed watcher always
    has, since setup deliberately never passes --budget -- while
    --max-sessions, the cap that actually binds it, was not logged at all.

  * status hard-coded five component names, so a component setup reported as
    FAILED (entities, say) was missing from status entirely, despite the
    component ids being declared as one shared vocabulary.

Adds scripts/trial-setup.sh: one command that runs the whole first-run
experience against a synthesised throwaway repository with HOME, the XDG
dirs, the plugin dirs and both daemon knobs redirected into a sandbox,
exercises the failure modes (non-repository, offline, two concurrent setups),
and proves on teardown that the machine's launchd/systemd state is unchanged.","messageHeadline":"fix(setup): make the first run report only the failures a user caused","oid":"9ab541f218ccd4fd5d890b6bab02654545f66677"},{"authoredDate":"2026-09-05T23:32:33Z","authors":[{"email":"r@r","id":"","login":"","name":"r"}],"committedDate":"2026-09-05T23:32:33Z","messageBody":"Finish writes its one permanent line onto the SAME physical row the
in-place repaints own, but it was the only writer of that row that did
not budget its width. liveLine has truncated its label from the start,
and terminalWidth's own comment already spells out why: the
carriage-return erase clears exactly one physical row, so a line wider
than the terminal wraps and the wrapped remainder survives every later
erase, stranded on screen under the final line.

A successful instant phase produces exactly that. On a 120-column
terminal the real label

    instant core ready in 1m4.4s - built sessions, seed, docs, semantic,
    patterns, entities, memory; the brain is queryable now done

measures 130 cells. Seven components is the ordinary outcome, not a
pathological input, so this fires on a normal first run.

Budget the line the same way liveLine does, charging the mark glyph and
its separating space. tui gains MarkGlyph for it: the width has to be
measured on the PLAIN glyph, because measuring the painted form charges
the SGR bytes as display width.

Only the terminal line is truncated. The permanent summary and status
rows are left alone deliberately - several of them carry absolute paths,
and clipping a path the reader is meant to copy is worse than a wrap on
a row nothing repaints over.","messageHeadline":"fix(progress): keep a task's terminal line inside the terminal","oid":"9e4baf0b6467c498d2acd2888fa4fcee0068a151"},{"authoredDate":"2026-09-05T23:32:48Z","authors":[{"email":"r@r","id":"","login":"","name":"r"}],"committedDate":"2026-09-05T23:32:48Z","messageBody":"trial-setup.sh answers "is this safe": it refuses a non-repository,
survives being offline, is idempotent, and leaks nothing. Nothing
answered "what does it look like", and the two cannot be the same
script - the trial runs against a tiny synthesised tree with no sessions
and no semantic provider, which is the fastest way to check behaviour
and the worst way to see it.

setup renders one in-place line: a braille spinner, a determinate bar
that colour-ramps across its cells as it fills, and a tick row of
components landing one by one. All of it is gated on the destination
being a terminal, so a piped run gets the deliberate degraded fallback -
whole lines, ASCII, no colour. This script therefore never pipes,
captures or tees the run, and refuses to start when stdout is not a
terminal rather than quietly demonstrating the fallback.

It arranges the three things a bare setup in a scratch directory lacks:

  - Real substance to index. The checkout is cloned (~1,200 tracked
    files, full history), so the semantic phase runs for about a minute
    rather than half a second and the repaints are visible.
  - A working entire-graph provider, installed INTO the sandbox.
    Without it the semantic component fails and the run ends on a red
    cross. `entire plugin install` honours the sandboxed HOME, so the
    developer's real plugin registry is untouched. The demo clone is
    given a github origin URL for the same reason: entire-brain and
    entire-graph agree on gh/<owner>/<name> but their no-remote
    fallbacks never agree, and a key mismatch rejects the snapshot.
    Nothing is fetched from it.
  - Captured sessions, and a stub agent to distill them with. The facts
    bar is distilled/total sessions; with no sessions it is an empty
    track that never moves. Sessions are seeded into the demo clone's
    checkpoint ref in the shape `entire` itself writes, then distilled
    in paced batches so the bar is watched filling instead of jumping
    from nothing to done.

No tokens are spent: the distill agent is a stub that reads the
transcript on stdin and prints fixed fact lines. Sandboxing and the
teardown leak-diff match trial-setup.sh, plus a check that entire-graph
was registered inside the sandbox and not in the real plugin root.

The demo clone also excludes the generated benchmark corpora from its
brain index. The provider correctly declines to parse minified JSON, but
every skipped file is then reported as a blind spot, which degrades
semantic completeness and ends an otherwise all-green run on a cross.
The checkout's own .brainignore already excludes the sibling generated
directories and simply does not list these two.","messageHeadline":"feat(scripts): add demo-setup.sh, a watchable setup run","oid":"7187092497b4baaa84217b02ea861f03d36a1625"},{"authoredDate":"2026-09-05T23:48:54Z","authors":[{"email":"suhaan@entire.io","id":"","login":"","name":"Suhaan Thayyil"}],"committedDate":"2026-09-05T23:52:08Z","messageBody":"…angement

scripts/install.sh required entire-graph to be a sibling checkout with that
exact name, and the README said so outright. A user who cloned one repository,
cloned under a different directory name, or ran from a worktree hit a dead end:
'entire-graph not found at ...; set ENTIRE_GRAPH_DIR to its checkout'.

The provider is now resolved by three routes, and the one taken is printed:

  1. $ENTIRE_GRAPH_DIR when set. An explicit override is used exactly as given;
     a value that is not an entire-graph checkout is a hard error rather than a
     silent fallback to something else.
  2. A checkout already on the machine -- siblings of this checkout and of the
     main worktree when this is a linked one, the route-3 cache, and the usual
     source directories under $HOME. A candidate is accepted only when
     cmd/entire-graph and scripts/install-local.sh are both present, so a
     directory that merely carries the name is skipped. Trusting the name is
     how the sibling constraint became a documented prerequisite.
  3. Otherwise a shallow clone of the public entireio/entire-graph into
     ${XDG_CACHE_HOME:-~/.cache}/entire-brain/entire-graph, reused and
     refreshed by later runs and kept usable when the network is not.

When no route can work it fails naming all three and how to satisfy each.
ENTIRE_INSTALL_OFFLINE=1 disables the clone; ENTIRE_GRAPH_REPO and
ENTIRE_GRAPH_CACHE redirect it.

Prerequisites are now checked before anything is built and every missing one is
reported in a single pass with its fix: git, the entire CLI, a Go toolchain at
least as new as the go directive in go.mod (tolerating an older go when
GOTOOLCHAIN may fetch the newer one), and a C compiler for entire-graph's
tree-sitter cgo bindings. A missing compiler previously surfaced minutes into a
build.

scripts/bootstrap.sh is the same flow for a machine with nothing: it uses the
checkout it was run from when there is one, otherwise clones entire-brain,
falling back to gh repo clone for the private-repo credentials, then execs
install.sh. There is no curl | sh form on purpose -- entireio/entire-brain is
private so raw.githubusercontent.com answers 404 without a token, the install
is a source build so the clone happens either way, and cloning first puts the
script that registers the plugins on disk at a reviewable commit before it runs.

README, docs/getting-started.md and docs/operations.md lead with the one command,
keep the two-clone path below it, state that Go 1.26 and cgo are still required,
say what the installer does to the machine, and drop the 'directory names
matter' constraint now that it is no longer true.","messageHeadline":"feat(install): make installing from git one command with no prior arr…","oid":"46dd2168cd28eb62a6f4e8dd6fc75eef4f4d69e2"},{"authoredDate":"2026-09-06T00:05:54Z","authors":[{"email":"r@r","id":"","login":"","name":"r"}],"committedDate":"2026-09-06T00:24:19Z","messageBody":"demo-setup.sh defaulted the provider checkout to $repo_root/../entire-graph,
which was an artifact of the directory it was written in. Any checkout not
parked beside an entire-graph clone -- a linked worktree, for one -- got a dead
stop on step 1 with nothing to do but set an environment variable. A demo that

The provider is now resolved by the same three routes scripts/install.sh uses,
under the same variable names, and the run reports which one it took:
ENTIRE_GRAPH_DIR when set (honoured exactly -- a wrong value is an error, not a
reason to look elsewhere), then a checkout already on this machine, then a

Candidates are confirmed by content rather than by directory name, and the
search covers the sibling of the main worktree -- where a paired checkout

that has already installed does not fetch a second copy. Resolution runs before

Two more assumptions about where this runs went with it. $0-relative repo_root
derivation is now resolved through symlinks and verified to be an entire-brain

plugin-registration leak check asserted a single hard-coded plugin layout; it
now searches the sandbox home, so it cannot fail on a correct run that chose the

README said "That is the whole install" and
the next runnable thing a reader was handed was `entire brain refresh --agent
none`; `entire brain setup` appeared only as an aside two sections later. And
docs/getting-started.md -- a guide whose whole job is the journey -- never

The install is machine-scoped: it registers two plugins and gives no repository
a brain. `entire brain setup` is what a person then runs inside a repository.
That second command is now the documented next step everywhere.

README:

  - new step 3a documents prerequisites and ordering from the code: the ONE

    side effect) versus everything `setup` degrades around -- `entire enable`,
    captured sessions, the graph provider, a service manager, an agent CLI --
    plus the real order (`entire enable` then `setup`) and the fact that a

  - the watcher is stated as what it is: a persistent launchd/systemd service

docs/getting-started.md: "First run" becomes "Onboard a repository: `entire

Three failures a new user hits on their first-ever `entire-brain setup`, all
found by running the real chain -- `entire enable`, an agent session, its hooks,
a checkpoint written by the post-commit hook, then setup -- rather than by
seeding a checkpoint ref with git plumbing. None of them can occur in
scripts/demo-setup.sh, which synthesises the ref and never runs `entire enable`.

1. A dirty worktree had no remedy. `entire enable` writes .entire/settings.json
   and the agent's .claude/settings.json and does not commit them, so the very
   next `entire-brain setup` -- the documented next step -- finds a dirty
   worktree and refuses to seed or index it. The refusal names `--worktree`, a
   flag `setup` does not accept, leaving the reader told to pass something they
   cannot pass, about files they never edited. Both refusals now share
   dirtyWorktreeErrorCode and setup attaches the remedy: commit or stash, and
   why the tree is dirty in the first place.

2. A repository with no sessions yet read as a fault. Between `entire enable`
   and the first finished session there are no checkpoints, and with the
   checkpoint remote unreachable the brain cannot prove the inventory is empty
   rather than unreadable -- so it reported "Entire returned no readable
   checkpoint IDs from an incomplete persistent-store inventory". True, and
   useless. The detail survives for anyone debugging a real fault; the hint says
   what the state means and how to check it. A routed discovery that genuinely
   failed keeps its own detail and is not softened into "you probably have no
   sessions yet".

3. `setup` did not build the history projection, then told the user to run
   `brief`. setup and a watch tick share one deterministic refresh path, and
   setup inherited the tick's decision to leave the durable projection to the
   memory coordinator -- correct for something that runs every few minutes,
   wrong for a one-shot onboarding build that ends by recommending `brief`. The
   first brief after a first-ever setup dropped its transcript half and printed
   "history index missing; run `entire brain refresh`": setup's own recommended
   next command reporting a gap in setup's own output. The two callers now say
   which behaviour they want.

   That change surfaced a fourth state, and the guard for it ships here too. On
   a first run every deterministic source can fail at once -- no sessions to
   export, and the worktree enable left dirty blocks the seed baseline -- and
   then there is no brain directory for the projector to read. It failed with
   "lstat <brainDir>: no such file or directory", answering "you have no
   sessions yet" with a rawer line naming an internal path. refresh now skips
   the projection when its target does not exist; an empty index over a brain
   directory that does exist is still built, as TestRefreshSeedsWhenExportFinds-
   NoSessions pins.

Each fix has a regression test in setup_firstrun_test.go that fails on a
compile-clean revert.","messageHeadline":"fix(setup): make the first run explain the states `entire enable` lea…","oid":"f7aab7d16131672fefe67ae71839c9137272fe85"},{"authoredDate":"2026-09-06T01:35:18Z","authors":[{"email":"r@r","id":"","login":"","name":"r"}],"committedDate":"2026-09-06T01:35:18Z","messageBody":"scripts/demo-setup.sh proves setup can read a checkpoint ref: it writes one into
the demo repository with git plumbing and runs setup over it. What it cannot
prove is the chain that produces the ref --

  entire enable -> an agent session -> the session-end hook -> a checkpoint ref
                -> entire-brain setup -> distill -> the brain answers

-- four components and three seams, none of them exercised by a synthesised ref,
and every bug this feature has shipped lived on one of them.

This script runs the whole chain against the real `entire` CLI in a sandbox and
ASSERTS at each seam, so it fails loudly rather than printing a green summary
over a broken link: `entire enable` must leave a session-end hook behind, the
session must leave a checkpoint ref behind, `entire checkpoint list` must read it
back, setup's manifest must report a non-zero session count, and `brief` must
return BOTH the exported transcript and the fact distilled from it. Every step
prints its command and its exit code.

Real and running here: `entire enable`; the git hooks and agent hook settings it
installs; the host CLI's own lifecycle hook verbs (`entire hooks claude-code
session-start|user-prompt-submit|stop|session-end`); the session state machine
behind them; the post-commit hook that writes the persistent checkpoint; `entire
checkpoint list`; setup, distill, status, overview and brief.

Substituted, and the only substitution: the model. A live agent would spend
tokens, so the script writes the transcript and hands it to the real hooks
exactly as the agent host would -- the hook contract is a JSON object on stdin
naming a transcript path, so nothing downstream can tell the difference. Zero
tokens are spent at any step. e2e/vogon in the entireio/cli checkout is the org's
closest tokenless agent, and is not used because it needs a second checkout to
build and `entire enable` refuses it by design (agent.IsTestOnly).

Sandboxing goes one variable further than demo-setup.sh: ENTIRE_CONFIG_DIR, on
top of HOME, the four XDG_*, the four ENTIRE_PLUGIN_*, ENTIRE_BRAIN_DAEMON_DIR
and ENTIRE_BRAIN_DAEMON_NO_REGISTER=1. `entire enable` is the one step that
writes outside the repository, and teardown diffs the real config store as well
as launchd/systemd state.","messageHeadline":"feat(scripts): add demo-agent-session.sh, the loop run for real","oid":"cec5512dca5846dec027dcfea9330053c6cd96fe"},{"authoredDate":"2026-09-06T01:35:29Z","authors":[{"email":"r@r","id":"","login":"","name":"r"}],"committedDate":"2026-09-06T01:35:29Z","messageBody":"…nd it

The install->setup journey now ends at a brain, but it stops short of the loop
that makes the brain worth having: nothing said what produces a checkpoint, or
that `entire enable` and `entire brain setup` do not compose in the order they
are written in.

- §3a's ordering block gains the step between the two commands. `entire enable`
  writes .entire/settings.json and the agent's hook settings and leaves them
  uncommitted, so `setup` run immediately afterwards refuses to seed or index a
  dirty worktree -- two red x on a first run, caused by the line above. Both
  files are project configuration, so committing them is the fix rather than a
  workaround. (`--worktree`, which the refusal names, is a `refresh` flag;
  `setup` does not accept it.)

- §3e documents scripts/demo-agent-session.sh: what it proves that demo-setup.sh
  cannot, exactly which components are real and which one is substituted, and
  the two facts about checkpoints the docs never stated -- `entire checkpoint`
  has no verb that creates one (the post-commit hook writes it, so the commit is
  part of the loop), and a freshly enabled repository uses one ref per
  checkpoint under refs/entire/checkpoints/, not the aggregate v1 branch
  demo-setup.sh seeds.

- §3f is the whole journey in one block: every command in order, with a table of
  which steps spend tokens and which install a persistent service. Two of the
  spends are recurring and neither prompts -- the watcher setup installs, and
  the session-end hook `entire enable` wires -- so both are named alongside the
  command that removes them.","messageHeadline":"docs(readme): document the journey through an agent session, not arou…","oid":"917e5320bfea6c0ed0b516c459d17db530af1821"},{"authoredDate":"2026-09-06T04:01:09Z","authors":[{"email":"r@r","id":"","login":"","name":"r"}],"committedDate":"2026-09-06T04:01:09Z","messageBody":"…nattended

scripts/demo-agent-session.sh hung indefinitely partway through, twice, at ~42
and ~59 minutes. Under a captured pty its stdout is a terminal, so `entire
checkpoint list` paged its output through $PAGER -- `less` by default
(cmd/entire/cli/explain.go, outputWithPager -> buildPagerCmd) -- which then sat
on "Press RETURN to continue" with nobody there to press it.

sandbox() is the single place every `entire` and `entire-brain` invocation in
both demo scripts passes through, and `env -i` makes it the only source of a
child's environment, so the fix belongs there rather than on whichever command
happens to page today: PAGER=cat and GIT_PAGER=cat for output,
GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0 for input.

GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0 also closes a second, quieter hang. Once `entire enable`
has run, every later `git commit` in the demo runs Entire's git hooks, and the
prepare-commit-msg hook asks "Link this commit to session context?" on
/dev/tty -- the controlling terminal, which no input redirection can answer.
Both commits also ran outside sandbox(), handing those hook children the
developer's real HOME and ENTIRE_CONFIG_DIR. They now run through sandbox(),
where the CLI reads GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0 as "this caller cannot answer
prompts" (cmd/entire/cli/interactive/interactive.go, isAgentSubprocessEnv) and
auto-links instead of asking -- the prompt's own default, so the commit is
still linked to its checkpoint.

The unreachable-remote warning `entire checkpoint list` prints is left exactly
as it is and narrated instead. It is a true report of this demo's deliberately
unreachable origin, and the same message in a real run is precisely what a user
with a broken checkpoint remote needs to see.

internal/cli/demo_scripts_test.go guards both invariants: nothing else in the
build or the suite notices if the env entries or the sandboxed commits are
dropped again.","messageHeadline":"fix(demo): keep every demo child non-blocking so the scripts finish u…","oid":"f769e9b1d3fa74174dd3f075a054585cdcafc822"},{"authoredDate":"2026-09-06T14:27:54Z","authors":[{"email":"suhaan@entire.io","id":"","login":"","name":"Suhaan Thayyil"}],"committedDate":"2026-09-06T14:27:54Z","messageBody":"`entire brain setup` failed its semantic component on every repository
created with `git init`, and the hint it printed blamed the reader's
repository for a disagreement between two of our own tools:

  x semantic index: repo key mismatch: semantic snapshot repo_key
    "local/myproject" does not match current repo "local/myproject-459a916099fb"
    hint: this repo has no git remote; add one (git remote add origin ...)
          or upgrade the entire CLI so both derive the same key

The two sides name the same repository by different rules. entire-graph
(internal/sem/provider.go) recognises github.com remotes and nothing else,
falling back to the literal `"local/" + filepath.Base(absRepo)` of the
--repo path it is handed. The brain (internal/cli/env.go) recognises many
hosts by slug and, for a repository with no usable remote, derives
`local/<basename>-<sha256(abs path)[:12]>`.

Measured, one snapshot per shape, against the installed provider:

  no remote        provider local/myproject   brain local/myproject-<12hex>  MISMATCH
  github.com       provider gh/acme/proj      brain gh/acme/proj             match
  gitlab.com       provider local/gl-proj     brain gl/acme/gl-proj          MISMATCH
  bitbucket.org    provider local/bb-proj     brain bb/acme/bb-proj          MISMATCH

So the defect is wider than "no git remote": every non-GitHub origin hits
it too, and the hint fires on repositories that already have the remote it
tells the reader to add. No upgrade of either tool would have reconciled
the two spellings.

Of the three available fixes this is the only one that survives contact.
Dropping the brain's hash suffix reintroduces what the suffix exists to
prevent: two checkouts sharing a basename would address ONE brain and
silently merge their histories. Moving entire-graph onto the brain's
suffix is a second repository whose repo key is baked into every symbol ID
and every cached index it has ever written. The brain, by contrast, can
fix this alone: it knows the provider's fallback rule and the exact --repo
path it handed the provider, so it can recognise the provider's spelling
of THIS repository and store the snapshot under its own key.

This is not a weakening of the crossover guard. The live path validates
the snapshot's commit and tree against this repository's HEAD immediately
after the key, and the provider was invoked by this process on this very
directory; those checks are what actually prove the snapshot describes
this repository. repo_key equality was only ever asserting that two tools
spell a name the same way. A snapshot naming any OTHER repository is still
refused, with the provider's own key in the message — verified against a
snapshot the provider had cached under a previous origin, which is now the
only way this failure appears.

The relaxation is scoped to a snapshot the brain just built itself. Bundle
import and the stored-snapshot read-back still compare keys exactly, since
there the key is the only provenance there is; a caller that supplies no
repo key gets the header untouched.

A fresh `git init` repository now reaches an all-green setup with no user
action:

  Brain ready in 870ms
    repo        /tmp/v-plain  (local/v-plain-02611d99789c)
    instant     + sessions  + seed  + history  + docs  + semantic
                + patterns  + entities  + memory  (850ms)

README documented the mismatch as an expected condition on a new
repository. It is not one any more, so that guidance is replaced rather
than left as folklore.","messageHeadline":"fix(semantic): accept the provider's own spelling of this repository","oid":"b970794e674d19c8c53147e264c5647f1d233406"},{"authoredDate":"2026-09-06T14:28:15Z","authors":[{"email":"suhaan@entire.io","id":"","login":"","name":"Suhaan Thayyil"}],"committedDate":"2026-09-06T14:28:15Z","messageBody":"Two things setup printed were wrong for the reader in front of it.

FIRST, the vocabulary. The brain ships as a kubectl-style external command
of the Entire CLI, so a reader who types `entire brain setup` never types
the binary's own name — and on a managed install (`entire plugin install`)
they cannot: the binary lives in <xdg_data>/entire/plugins/bin, a
directory the Entire CLI prepends to PATH inside its OWN process and
nowhere else. Every command setup and status printed back was spelled
`entire-brain ...` regardless, so the closing Next block handed a plugin
reader three commands their shell cannot resolve.

The signal is the host's, not ours: the Entire CLI's plugin dispatcher
sets ENTIRE_CLI_VERSION in the child's environment unconditionally on
every plugin launch. It is the only unconditional one — ENTIRE_REPO_ROOT
is set only inside a worktree, ENTIRE_PLUGIN_DATA_DIR is dropped when the
data dir cannot be resolved — and os.Args[0] is no signal at all, because
the dispatcher execs the resolved binary path. Absent it the standalone
name stays, which is the honest answer: that reader may not have the host
CLI. setupCommandPrefix resolves the spelling once per run and it is
threaded to every printer as an explicit argument, so the summary's Next
block, every skip and failure line, all three hints, the status verdict
and its follow-ups, and setup --help move together and cannot drift apart
again. Both spellings are twelve cells wide, so every column budget in
these blocks holds by construction; a test pins that.

SECOND, the watcher. One `entire brain setup` on a brand-new repository
registers a persistent launchd agent in the user's real
~/Library/LaunchAgents and starts it, and the only mention of that arrived
mid-summary, after the fact — while --uninstall-daemon appeared only in
`setup --help`, and even there under a command name a plugin reader cannot
run. That tells the reader what was done TO their machine rather than what
is about to be.

The default is deliberately unchanged. Whether the watcher should install
unasked is a product decision and not this commit's to make. What this
commit does is make the consequence impossible to miss before it happens
and put its removal on the same screen: setup now opens with one line
naming the unit and its path, saying plainly that it is a persistent
service that starts again at every login, and naming both the flag that
declines it and the command that removes it.

  setup: background watcher: this run will install
    io.entire.brain-watch.a2d3fd66 at ~/Library/LaunchAgents/
    io.entire.brain-watch.a2d3fd66.plist — a persistent launchd service
    that starts again at every login; pass --no-daemon to skip it, or
    remove it later with `entire brain setup --uninstall-daemon`

It is the first line of the run, before any work. A re-run that finds the
service already there says "keeps ... installed" instead: "will install"
on every setup is a line readers stop reading. --no-daemon installs
nothing and so says nothing, and a platform with no service manager has
nothing to announce. The daemon phase still inspects for itself, so its
idempotence decision is made on the state as it is then rather than on
this observation from before the instant and backfill phases.

The repo-key hint is rewritten here too: its old text ("this repo has no
git remote; add one ... or upgrade the entire CLI") described a condition
the previous commit removed, and fired on repositories that had a remote.","messageHeadline":"fix(setup): say what will be installed, in the words the reader typed","oid":"6676459d4890fc91515bbdb02af45852d5f6d528"},{"authoredDate":"2026-09-06T14:43:42Z","authors":[{"email":"r@r","id":"","login":"","name":"r"}],"committedDate":"2026-09-06T14:43:42Z","messageBody":"`docs/getting-started.md` still told a first-time reader to expect
`Brain ready (degraded)` on a repository new to Entire, and named two
components as the cause. Both halves are wrong now.

`x semantic index: repo key mismatch` is fixed: the brain accepts the
provider's own spelling of the repository it just asked the provider to
index, so a fresh `git init` repository reaches an all-green setup with
no user action. The guide's framing was also never right about WHY --
"the repository has no git remote" -- because every non-GitHub origin
hit the same mismatch, and the advice it gave (`git remote add origin`)
fired on repositories that already had one.

`x session export` is not the second cause either. Verified against the
branch binary on a scratch repository, with and without `entire enable`,
online and offline: the export returns an empty inventory and the
`sessions` component is GREEN. It fails only when Entire cannot prove
the inventory is empty rather than merely unreadable -- a configured
checkpoint remote it cannot enumerate -- which is a real fault with its
own hint, not the state every new repository is in.

What the guide says instead is what the binary prints, quoted from real
runs: the all-green summary block, the dirty-worktree refusal `entire

{"additions":16964,"author":{"id":"U_kgDOD1cBdA","is_bot":false,"login":"suhaanthayyil","name":"Suhaan Thayyil"},"baseRefName":"main","body":"One command per machine, one per repository. `entire brain setup` builds a queryable
brain in about a second, and this PR is mostly the work of making that true for a person
who has never seen the tool before.

## The journey, verified end to end

```sh
# once per machine
git clone https://github.com/entireio/entire-brain.git
entire-brain/scripts/install.sh

# once per repository
cd /path/to/your/repo
entire brain setup
```

Run on a clean clone at `52a4bf81` (this branch merged with `main`), against a fresh
`git init` repository with **no remote** — the shape that used to fail:

```
Brain ready in 870ms
  repo        /Users/…/proj  (local/proj-966f22b7fb9b)
  instant     + sessions  + seed  + history  + docs  + semantic  + patterns  + entities  + memory  (840ms)
  facts       .............. 0/0 sessions distilled
  workspace   + default  (30ms)
  daemon      - skipped: --no-daemon  (0s)

Next
  entire brain overview        what this project is
  entire brain brief "<task>"  task-shaped context
  entire brain status          backfill progress and daemon health
```

`install.sh` 5.4s · `setup` 870ms · `status`, `overview`, `brief` all exit 0 ·
`brief` returns repo-derived content (`symbol Greet greet/greet.go:3-8`).

## What was broken

Every item below was found by **running the product as a user**, not by reading it. The
demo scripts in this PR passed clean and caught none of the first six.

### Nobody could install it

`scripts/install.sh` hardcoded `../entire-graph`, and the README said outright *"The
directory names matter."* Clone one repo, rename a directory, or work from a worktree and
you hit a dead end. It now resolves the provider three ways — explicit `ENTIRE_GRAPH_DIR`,
a discovered checkout **verified by content rather than by folder name**, or a shallow
clone from git — and `scripts/bootstrap.sh` covers starting from nothing. Preflight
reports every missing prerequisite at once instead of dying on the first, partway through
a build.

Piped-curl was considered and rejected: this repo is private, so `curl | sh` would mean
"export a token, then pipe an unread script into your shell", and the install is a source
build so the clone happens either way.

### The docs stopped at the install

`README.md` said *"That is the whole install"* and never mentioned `entire brain setup`.
`docs/getting-started.md` mentioned it **zero times in 762 lines** — it sent readers to
`refresh` instead. A person finished with working plugins and no idea what to do in their
own repository.

The old prerequisites were also wrong, which the code settles: `setup` needs **a git
repository** and nothing else. `entire enable` is not required, and `setup` deliberately
will not do it — from `setup_status.go`, *"hook registration belongs to the Entire CLI's
repository enablement … Duplicating it here would produce two hooks racing to distill the
same session."*

### `entire enable` and `entire brain setup` do not compose

`enable` writes `.entire/` and `.claude/` and **leaves them uncommitted**, so the very
next `setup` refuses to seed or index a dirty worktree — two red ✗ caused by the command
directly above it. The real order is `enable` → **commit** → `setup`, now documented with
the reason, and the refusal carries a remedy that names a flag `setup` actually accepts.

### A fresh repository always failed the semantic component

```
x semantic index: repo key mismatch: semantic snapshot repo_key "local/myproject"
                  does not match current repo "local/myproject-459a916099fb"
```

`entire-brain` derives `<base>-sha256(abspath)[:12]`; `entire-graph` recognises only
github.com remotes and otherwise falls back to `local/<basename>`. Measured per origin:

| origin | provider | brain | |
|---|---|---|---|
| none | `local/proj` | `local/proj-<12hex>` | mismatch |
| github | `gh/acme/proj` | `gh/acme/proj` | match |
| gitlab | `local/gl-proj` | `gl/acme/gl-proj` | mismatch |
| bitbucket | `local/bb-proj` | `bb/acme/bb-proj` | mismatch |

So it was never "no remote" — **every non-GitHub origin** hit it, while the hint told
repositories that already had a remote to add one, blaming the reader for a disagreement
between two of our own tools.

Fixed on the live path only: the brain accepts the provider's own fallback spelling of the
directory it just handed that provider, and stores the snapshot under its own key. Bundle
import and stored-snapshot read-back still compare keys exactly. This is not a weakened
guard — the live path validates commit and tree against HEAD immediately afterwards, and
key equality was only ever asserting that two tools spell a name alike.

Two alternatives were rejected for cause: dropping brain's suffix merges two same-basename
repositories' brains, and making the provider adopt the suffix invalidates every existing
index, because its repo key is baked into every `symbolID()`.

### `setup` recommended a command it had just broken

`setup` reused the watch tick's `historyIndex:false` — correct for a five-minute tick,
wrong for one-shot onboarding — so the first `brief` after the first `setup` printed
*"history index missing"* and silently dropped its transcript half.

### The output answered in the wrong vocabulary

You typed `entire brain setup`; the Next block replied `entire-brain overview`. Output now
follows how you invoked it, keyed on `ENTIRE_CLI_VERSION`, swept across every hint, error
and follow-up.

### Two hangs that would have stopped a reader dead

`entire checkpoint list` pages its output, and nothing set `PAGER`, so under a captured
terminal it blocked forever on *"Press RETURN to continue"* — reproduced twice, at 42 and
59 minutes. Separately, `git commit` after `entire enable` fires
`prepare-commit-msg`, which prompts on **`/dev/tty`**, not stdin: no redirection can answer
it. Both fixed at the sandbox boundary, so every child and grandchild inherits the fix.

## The daemon still installs unasked

`setup` installs a persistent launchd/systemd watcher **by default, with no prompt**, and
it restarts at every login. **That default is unchanged here — it is a product decision,
not one this PR should make quietly.** What changed is that it can no longer surprise you:

```
setup: background watcher: this run will install io.entire.brain-watch.a2d3fd66 at
~/Library/LaunchAgents/io.entire.brain-watch.a2d3fd66.plist — a persistent launchd service
that starts again at every login; pass --no-daemon to skip it, or remove it later with
`entire brain setup --uninstall-daemon`
```

That is the **first line of the run**, before any work. A re-run says *"this run keeps …
installed"*, and `--no-daemon` says nothing at all.

Worth weighing before merge: on a repository with real history the backfill distils 25
sessions immediately and 25 every 24 hours — roughly nine days of unattended agent spend
from one command typed once. `--no-backfill --no-daemon` spends nothing.

## Trying it

Three scripts, each sandboxed (`HOME`, all four `XDG_*`, all four `ENTIRE_PLUGIN_*`,
`ENTIRE_BRAIN_DAEMON_DIR`, `ENTIRE_BRAIN_DAEMON_NO_REGISTER=1`) with teardown that **diffs
`launchctl list` against a pre-run snapshot** rather than grepping, so your own watcher is
never mistaken for a leak. Zero token spend throughout — the backfill runs against a stub
agent.

| script | what it proves |
|---|---|
| `scripts/demo-agent-session.sh` | the **real loop**: `entire enable` → real git hooks → real commit → a genuine checkpoint ref → `setup` finds it → distill → `brief` answers from it. 28s, 13/13 steps exit 0. |
| `scripts/demo-setup.sh` | the UI under a real TTY: 10 cycling spinner frames, the facts bar filling through 6 states and colour-ramping `203`→`214`→`47`, ~669 in-place repaints, zero duplicate lines. 148s. |
| `scripts/trial-setup.sh` | safety: idempotence, offline, non-repository refusal, concurrent runs, leak checks. |

`demo-agent-session.sh` substitutes exactly one thing: **the model**. It writes the Claude
Code JSONL and hands it to the real hooks — the hook contract is
`{session_id, transcript_path, model}`, so nothing downstream can tell — but those
sentences were typed, not generated. Everything else is the real binary on real refs.

`demo-setup.sh` refuses to start if stdout is not a terminal, because every in-place
repaint and all colour are gated on `Caps.TTY`/`Caps.Color`. Piping it shows the degraded
fallback, which is the exact mistake that made this UI look unbuilt for weeks.

## Verification

On `52a4bf81` — this branch merged with `main`, 0 behind:

- `go build ./...` clean; `go test ./... -count=1` **exit 0**, all 10 packages
  (`internal/cli` 161.7s)
- `gofmt -s -l .` empty; `go vet ./...` clean
- the full user journey above, run from a clean clone against a remote-less repository
- `launchctl list` shows **0** `io.entire` jobs and `~/Library/LaunchAgents` **0** plists
  afterwards

Every behavioural change carries a regression test proven to fail on a **compile-clean
revert**, with the failing assertion quoted in its commit. No test was weakened or deleted;
where a fixture encoded the old behaviour it was corrected and the correction called out —
`newSetupTestFixture` modelled a directory that is *not* a git repository, which is the
exact state `setup` now rejects.

## Known and deliberately unfixed

- **entire-graph's index cache is tree-keyed, not repo-key-keyed.** Change a repository's
  `origin` without changing the tree and the provider replays the old snapshot under the
  old key. Reproduced; the fix here correctly still rejects that case and the hint points
  at `refresh index --force`. Provider-side bug, separate PR.
- **`scripts/` is not covered by CI's shellcheck** — it lints only `mise-tasks` and
  `.codex/hooks`. Both hangs above shipped through that gap.
- `entire brain refresh .` rejects a positional path where `setup` and `distill` accept
  one.

earlier one's. That is the right default, but it is wrong for a background
backfill: the pass is O(sessions) and the only output a user sees soon is its
first output, so the most recent — most useful — sessions must go first.

--newest-first reverses the visit order without changing the set of sessions
visited; the persisted distill cache means neither order re-spends on unchanged
sessions. --max-sessions caps how many uncached sessions one run distills. The
cap is enforced in the single in-order dispatcher, so the decision is
deterministic and no agent call is dispatched for a deferred session. Deferred
sessions stay uncached and are picked up by the next run — the budget defers
spend, it never drops a session.","messageHeadline":"feat(distill): add --newest-first ordering and a --max-sessions budget","oid":"38902251f131d3da426019c15557cac15a556651"},{"authoredDate":"2026-08-19T17:28:38Z","authors":[{"email":"257360244+suhaanthayyil@users.noreply.github.com","id":"U_kgDOD1cBdA","login":"suhaanthayyil","name":"Suhaan Thayyil"}],"committedDate":"2026-08-21T13:41:19Z","messageBody":"The watcher exists (`workspace watch`) but nothing installs it, so freshness
still depends on someone remembering to run it in a terminal that stays open.

This adds the install layer: one daemon identity that renders to a launchd
agent on macOS and a systemd user unit on Linux, plus install/uninstall/inspect
through the injectable CommandRunner. Everything that decides WHAT gets
installed takes the target OS as an argument rather than reading runtime.GOOS,
so both platforms' artifacts are golden-tested from one machine.

Rendered artifacts are byte-stable across runs (sorted env keys), which is what
lets "already installed and current" be decided by comparing the file on disk
against a freshly rendered plan. Install unloads before loading so a re-run
replaces a stale job instead of failing or registering a second one.

The plugin dirs and PATH are carried explicitly into the service environment: a
launchd/systemd job inherits almost nothing, and without them the daemon would
silently target a different brain store than the CLI that installed it.","messageHeadline":"feat(setup): add daemon install glue and detached process spawning","oid":"160bbb429a090fe6b7dc26e3412aec98a499967b"},{"authoredDate":"2026-08-19T17:28:51Z","authors":[{"email":"257360244+suhaanthayyil@users.noreply.github.com","id":"U_kgDOD1cBdA","login":"suhaanthayyil","name":"Suhaan Thayyil"}],"committedDate":"2026-08-21T13:41:19Z","messageBody":"Onboarding had three separate paths — build the brain, build it with an agent,
extract facts — and the wrong one was in the foreground. The pass that made the
brain useful immediately was the one people skipped, and the O(sessions) agent
pass was the one they waited on and then never ran again.

`setup` collapses that into three phases with honest cost labels:

  instant   the deterministic core, blocking, seconds, zero agent tokens. This
            is the same free path `watch` runs each tick with seed agent "none".
            When it returns the brain is queryable, and setup says so.
  backfill  distill over past sessions, newest first, detached in its own
            session so it survives the terminal, on the cheap model/effort and
            bounded by --backfill-budget. Skipped with one clear line when no
            agent CLI is on PATH, when no sessions are captured yet, or when
            everything is already distilled.
  daemon    the repo joins a workspace and ONE machine-wide watcher keeps every
            member fresh. A second setup in a second repo adds a member, not a
            second daemon.

Every phase is idempotent: a healthy, byte-identical, running watcher is left
strictly alone (reloading it would kill an in-flight refresh), a drifted unit is
rewritten, and an existing workspace member is detected rather than appended.
--no-daemon and --uninstall-daemon are the opt-outs.

Progress goes on the existing `status` verb rather than a new one: facts
distilled over sessions captured, daemon health with its last tick, and which
instant-phase components exist. Doctor stays the deep environment check.

setup reports the session-end hook's wiring but does not install it: hook
registration belongs to the Entire CLI's repository enablement, which owns the
whole lifecycle hook set, and duplicating it would leave two hooks racing to
distill the same session.","messageHeadline":"feat(setup): add `entire-brain setup`, the one-command onboarding path","oid":"30f36d3198d554c75fcc6ba575ceb687e79d58d5"},{"authoredDate":"2026-08-19T17:38:50Z","authors":[{"email":"257360244+suhaanthayyil@users.noreply.github.com","id":"U_kgDOD1cBdA","login":"suhaanthayyil","name":"Suhaan Thayyil"}],"committedDate":"2026-08-21T13:41:19Z","messageBody":"runDistill rejects concurrency <= 0, but the value only ever came from a cobra
flag default. The watcher's gated distill step and `hook session-end` both build
distillCommandOptions in Go, where that default never applies, so both were
rejected before making a single agent call:

    [watch] distill failed: --concurrency must be greater than 0
    session-end: distill skipped: --concurrency must be greater than 0

That is the entire token-spending path of `watch --distill` and the whole point
of the session-end write loop. --jobs looked like it covered this but is only a
reporting alias; the pipeline and the guard both read concurrency.

The watcher now derives concurrency from --jobs (its existing knob) and the hook
uses the standard default. After the fix the same invocation reports the real
condition instead of the guard:

    session-end: distill skipped: distillation requires an agent
    (codex or claude-code); none found on PATH","messageHeadline":"fix(distill): set concurrency for the two in-process distill callers","oid":"0e567b0011520e3c7dd5985ceb018836eb65361b"},{"authoredDate":"2026-08-19T17:38:50Z","authors":[{"email":"257360244+suhaanthayyil@users.noreply.github.com","id":"U_kgDOD1cBdA","login":"suhaanthayyil","name":"Suhaan Thayyil"}],"committedDate":"2026-08-21T13:41:19Z","messageBody":"A repo set up with a custom --daemon-name was invisible afterwards: `status`
built its daemon plan from the defaults, so it reported a running watcher as
"not installed", and `setup --uninstall-daemon` would have looked for a daemon
that was never installed while leaving the real one running.

setup now records the workspace and daemon name it used alongside the repo's
other state, and later reads inherit them. An explicit flag still wins.

Also separates history from health in the status line: the watch cursor is
written only by a watcher tick, so it survives an uninstall — "not installed;
last tick 4m ago" read as a contradiction and is now "not installed (last
watcher tick 4m ago)".","messageHeadline":"fix(setup): remember the workspace and daemon identity per repo","oid":"0ba501cf007ed39cfc27731a66ef50aeb17de1df"},{"authoredDate":"2026-08-19T18:33:58Z","authors":[{"email":"257360244+suhaanthayyil@users.noreply.github.com","id":"U_kgDOD1cBdA","login":"suhaanthayyil","name":"suhaanthayyil"}],"committedDate":"2026-08-21T13:42:03Z","messageBody":"`setup` starts two distill passes over the same brain within seconds of each
other by design: it spawns the detached backfill and then installs a watcher
whose first tick distills immediately. The brain write lock does not stop that
— it only wraps the flush at the END of a pass, so both processes make every
agent call first and only then serialize on writing the identical facts.

Add a distill-pass lock held for the whole pass and acquired try-only. Every
in-process caller funnels through runDistill (the detached backfill child, the
watcher's gated step, the session-end hook, a human running `distill`), so one
guard covers all of them. Try-only rather than blocking is the point: a second
comer must skip cleanly, not queue behind an hours-long backfill and then
re-spend on the sessions that backfill just finished.","messageHeadline":"fix(distill): hold a cross-process lock for the whole distill pass","oid":"4be67c663f6a372b3c154d57dbfa9d807439a33a"},{"authoredDate":"2026-08-19T18:34:16Z","authors":[{"email":"257360244+suhaanthayyil@users.noreply.github.com","id":"U_kgDOD1cBdA","login":"suhaanthayyil","name":"suhaanthayyil"}],"committedDate":"2026-08-21T13:42:03Z","messageBody":"Live review of the onboarding path found seven defects that only appear once
setup is actually run twice, on two repos, on a machine that stays up.

The installed watcher distilled once, ever. setup passed `--budget 1`, but
--budget counts gated agent runs for the life of the process and never resets,
and the unit is a KeepAlive service that never exits — so one machine spent
once, forever, across every repo in the workspace, while reporting itself
healthy. Drop --budget from the daemon argv and rely on --distill-every plus
each repo's persisted cursor, the durable guard that bounds spend per repo per
window without latching off. The replacement test simulates three windows over
two repos through the real installed argv and asserts six gated runs.

Re-running setup mid-backfill spawned a second detached pass over the same
pending sessions. Consult the recorded state and pid first: report the running
pass and its progress, and skip.

A bare `setup` distilled the whole corpus. --backfill-budget now defaults to 25
sessions per pass, newest first, and setup prints what the cap did and how to
lift it; 0 keeps its meaning as an explicit "the whole corpus in one spend".

Setting up a second repo restarted the daemon. The machine-wide unit embedded
the calling repo's log path, so every new repo rendered different bytes, which
inspectDaemon correctly read as drift and repaired by unloading and reloading
the running watcher. The daemon log moves to a machine-level path.

Concurrent setups lost workspace registrations: the manifest was
read-modify-written with no lock. All membership changes now go through one
locked path that also decides created/already inside the lock.

`status` claimed the session-end hook was wired when it belonged to some other
tool — any non-empty SessionEnd command satisfied the check. Verify the command
invokes the Entire CLI's hook, report which command matched, and separately
report whether `entire` is on PATH; a hook naming a binary this machine does
not have is worse than no hook.

A re-run silently reverted daemon customisations. "Did the user pass this
flag?" was answered by comparing against defaults, which cannot tell an
explicit default from silence. Read Flags().Changed instead, remember
interval/distill-every/model/effort alongside the workspace and daemon name,
and unload the old unit when --daemon-name changes, so a rename moves the
daemon instead of forking it.

Also in the install glue: launchd labels carry a digest of the full daemon name
(trimming the "entire-" prefix alone mapped two names onto one job and one
plist); systemd values are escaped rather than quoted for the single-value
settings systemd does not unquote (WorkingDirectory=, StandardOutput=,
StandardError= are parsed without EXTRACT_UNQUOTE, so a quote becomes part of
the path and the setting is rejected — what they need is `%` escaped as `%%`,
and newlines refused outright); and the unit path honours
ENTIRE_BRAIN_DAEMON_DIR so a sandboxed run cannot install a live agent into a
real user's directories even when it can see the real $HOME.","messageHeadline":"fix(setup): stop the watcher latching off and the daemon churning","oid":"8c7b0c62f23041b958d79f85983f2fdce9e815c2"},{"authoredDate":"2026-08-19T18:34:27Z","authors":[{"email":"257360244+suhaanthayyil@users.noreply.github.com","id":"U_kgDOD1cBdA","login":"suhaanthayyil","name":"suhaanthayyil"}],"committedDate":"2026-08-21T13:42:03Z","messageBody":"Setting concurrency for the two in-process distill callers fixed a real bug —
both left the field at zero, so runDistill rejected every gated distill either
of them ever attempted before making a single agent call. That also turned two
dead paths into live, recurring spend: an installed watcher now calls an agent
once per --distill-every per repo, and a wired session-end hook distills the
session that just ended. The gating did not change; what changed is that the
gates are now reached.

Say so where people will see it: a setup section in the README with a
phase/cost table and the four gates that bound it, the same disclosure in the
command's help, and a CHANGELOG recording the behaviour change alongside the
defects fixed in this pass.","messageHeadline":"docs: disclose the token spend setup turns on","oid":"f75dc1b482ee9cd0eec7645f2958c45e79ac11b0"},{"authoredDate":"2026-08-19T19:24:21Z","authors":[{"email":"257360244+suhaanthayyil@users.noreply.github.com","id":"U_kgDOD1cBdA","login":"suhaanthayyil","name":"suhaanthayyil"}],"committedDate":"2026-08-21T14:01:21Z","messageBody":"…ding

The instant phase was all-or-nothing: `steps.instant` returned one error and
runSetup returned it. On a local repo with no git remote the semantic step
fails with `semantic snapshot repo_key "local/repo" does not match current repo
"local/repo-<hash>"` — a pre-existing key-derivation skew between the installed
entire CLI and the brain — and that one component took the whole run with it.
No workspace, no daemon, no status, on a brain whose other four sources had
built perfectly. First-run UX died on a component failure.

The instant phase is now per-component best-effort. runRefresh gained an
optional `component` callback that reports each stage's outcome and stops the
first failure from aborting the run; setup collects those outcomes, prints one
line per degraded component ("semantic index failed (...) — continuing; run
'entire-brain doctor' for detail"), and carries on to the backfill, the
workspace registration and the daemon install. The phase summary names what
built and what failed.

setup exits non-zero only when nothing usable exists: the phase could not run at
all, or every component it attempted failed — then with every reason it
collected. The rule is documented in the command help.

The repo-key mismatch gets the hint its error text lacks: add a remote, or
upgrade the CLI so both sides derive the same key.

The outcome is persisted per repo, so `status` reports semantic=failed rather
than semantic=missing (a failed source and one nobody attempted need opposite
reactions, and the skew leaves a stale snapshot on disk that presence checks
read as built), and `doctor` prints the reason. A source rebuilt since the
recorded failure reads built again, so a stale record cannot pin a healthy
brain as broken.","messageHeadline":"fix(setup): degrade on a failing component instead of aborting onboar…","oid":"59b24946be323ab02d0046e519c47cb9675652cd"},{"authoredDate":"2026-08-19T21:23:56Z","authors":[{"email":"257360244+suhaanthayyil@users.noreply.github.com","id":"U_kgDOD1cBdA","login":"suhaanthayyil","name":"suhaanthayyil"}],"committedDate":"2026-08-21T14:01:21Z","messageBody":"The windows job failed eight tests in two classes, both caused by the same
mistake: taking goos as an argument but then letting the HOST decide what that
argument means.

Golden tests (darwin/linux plans): the unit path was built with filepath.Join,
whose separator is the host's, so a darwin plan rendered on a windows runner
came out as \Users\demo\Library\LaunchAgents\... — a path no mac would accept.
Paths in a launchd/systemd plan describe a POSIX machine and are now joined
with path.Join, keyed to the goos argument like everything else in the plan.

Setup daemon-flow tests: runSetup resolved its plan through runtime.GOOS, so on
windows every install/idempotence/retirement assertion saw an unsupported plan
and read installs == 0. The plan is now an injectable step, so those properties
are tested from any host, and brainWatchDaemonPlanFor keeps runtime.GOOS to a
single call site.

Windows behaviour is made explicit rather than incidental: with no launchd and
no systemd, setup skips the daemon phase in one line naming the platform and
the manual `workspace watch` alternative, reports manager=unsupported in the
JSON report, and retires nothing. New tests pin both the skip line and the
report, planning for "windows" so they run everywhere.

Also close a test-isolation gap: the fixtures redirected HOME but not
USERPROFILE (which os.UserHomeDir reads on windows) or ENTIRE_BRAIN_DAEMON_DIR,
so a developer with a live daemon dir exported failed
TestBuildBrainOnboardingStatusReportsBackfillAndDaemon locally while CI passed.

The
commands people actually run — setup, status — write ordinary lines to a
stream that may be a terminal, a pipe, a CI log, a systemd journal, or a
hook whose stdout is contractually empty. They deserve colour, marks,
spinners and bars when the destination can render them, and byte-stable
plain text when it cannot.

Caps answers "what can THIS stream render" explicitly: TTY, colour
(NO_COLOR and TERM=dumb each disable it independently), unicode (gated on
the locale, so a non-UTF-8 terminal never receives a braille spinner or an
em dash and draws a replacement box instead of it), and width. It is
injectable, so the four-way matrix is testable without a real terminal.

Escape sequences are emitted directly rather than through lipgloss, whose
colour profile is a package global bound to os.Stdout — neither the stream
being written to, nor stable under `go test`. The palette is still this
package's Theme, extended with a second accent so a line renderer can
colour-code more states than the dashboard's four.

Terminal width falls back to COLUMNS and then to 80 rather than reporting
"unknown": an untruncated live line wraps, and a carriage-return erase only
clears the last physical row.

Entire-Checkpoint: 002c20362cca","messageHeadline":"feat(tui): add a capability-gated line renderer","oid":"4b306e7f01a9e90603b4c3e97b3ffafeb0020cd4"},{"authoredDate":"2026-08-21T15:12:55Z","authors":[{"email":"257360244+suhaanthayyil@users.noreply.github.com","id":"U_kgDOD1cBdA","login":"suhaanthayyil","name":"suhaanthayyil"}],"committedDate":"2026-08-21T15:12:55Z","messageBody":"Three reported glitches, all in the progress renderer:

1. Every phase printed TWICE. The plain path printed on Begin, again on
   every Update, and again on Finish, so the overwhelmingly common
   `task.Update(summary); task.Finish(nil)` pair emitted the summary once
   bare and once with " done" bolted on. A task now announces itself when
   it starts, buffers later labels, and emits exactly one line per distinct
   phase — the last one carrying the outcome. A task that succeeds without
   ever changing its label prints once, not twice; a failure always prints.

2. A stray glyph mid-line on terminals whose locale is not UTF-8. Every
   spinner frame, mark, bar cell, dash and separator now comes from the
   renderer's locale-gated glyph set, with an ASCII fallback.

3. The semantic phase flooded and flickered. Its label carries running
   counters that change every few hundred records, and the status key only
   folded "N/M unit" and ", N sessions" — so every callback read as a new
   phase. Repaints are now capped at ten per second and plain-mode labels
   that differ only in their numbers are coalesced. A per-item COMPLETION
   (one distilled session) goes through Event instead, which never
   coalesces: that heartbeat is the only progress a detached backfill log
   has.

Underneath all three: in-place rendering is now owned by one process-wide
line. setup painted a spinner on stdout while the refresh it calls painted
its own on stderr; both rewrote the same physical row, neither erased the
other, and a line wider than the terminal wrapped into a visible duplicate.
Only the innermost task paints, the suspended outer one is erased and
repainted when it comes back, ordinary output goes through
printAroundLiveLine, and every live line is truncated to the terminal
width so it can never wrap. Finish is idempotent, because a second
terminal line for one task is the same bug one call site further along.

Tasks can also carry a determinate count, which renders as a colour-ramped
bar: checkpoint export and the history index report real totals, and the
semantic stream now reports its running file count so its bar is scaled by
the previous generation's file count rather than left indeterminate.

Each phase gets one in-place line
carrying a spinner, a colour-ramped bar where a real count exists
(checkpoint export, history index, semantic files) and a per-component
tick row that fills in as components land rather than revealing all of
them when the phase returns. Phases are colour-coded — instant, backfill,
daemon, done, skipped, failed — and the run closes on a summary block with
a per-component mark row, the failure detail and hint underneath, a facts

Timings are render-only and deliberately absent from setupReport: `setup
--json` is a published contract and a new field in it is a breaking change
for anything parsing it today. A golden test pins the --json bytes of both
setup and status against captures taken before any of this existed.

status stopped being usable. On a repository that vendors JSON corpora it
printed forty-four "partial failure: E_MINIFIED" lines, then the SAME
forty-four files again as blind spots, then a twenty-three entry
relation-type histogram: about 130 lines, of which six answered a question
anyone had. So:

  - The default report is short: identity, the onboarding block (fact
    backfill with a mini bar, daemon state, instant components as a mark
    row) and a one-line health verdict.
  - --verbose prints the full report, with repeated warnings collapsed to
    one line per reason and no record listed twice across sections. Files
    that are obviously data — a JSON corpus, a lockfile, a sourcemap, a
    minified bundle — are grouped as "N data files skipped" rather than
    enumerated; a blind spot that is real source is still named
    individually, because that one has to be acted on.
  - doctor prints the full grouped list, which is where the short report
    now points.

All of it degrades to plain, byte-stable ASCII when stdout is not a
terminal, honours NO_COLOR, and leaves --json untouched.
